     1	// reference/src/semantics/call.k — MPY-CALL
     2	// ONE call route for every callable: evaluate the callee to a VALUE (name lookup reaches
     3	// builtins at the root; a cooled Attribute is a bound method), evaluate the args (the shared
     4	// #evalArgs loop in core.k), then dispatch on the callee value:
     5	//   closureVal    -> bind params, push a frame (user function)
     6	//   boundMethodV  -> applyMethod
     7	//   builtinV      -> the #iterNext folds (sum/all/any/max/min) or applyBuiltin
     8	//   typeV         -> callable type objects: int(...) / str(...)
     9	
    10	module MPY-CALL
    11	  imports MPY-METHODS
    12	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    13	  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
    14	
    15	  // a cooled attribute is a bound method value
    16	  rule <k> Attribute(V:Val, M:String) => boundMethodV(V, M) ... </k>
    17	
    18	  // evaluate callee, then args ([owise]: problem-local Call interceptions beat this)
    19	  syntax KItem ::= #callee(Exprs)
    20	  rule <k> Call(Fe:Expr, ARGS:Exprs) => Fe ~> #callee(ARGS) ... </k> [owise]
    21	  rule <k> CV:Val ~> #callee(ARGS:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ARGS, .Vals, toCall(CV)) ... </k>
    22	
    23	  // ==== dispatch on the callee value ========================================
    24	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyMethod(OBJ, M, ACC) ... </k>
    25	
    26	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sum")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #sumAcc(OBJ, 0) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("all")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #allAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("any")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #anyAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    29	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("max")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #maxAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("min")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #minAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(BN, ACC) ... </k> [owise]
    32	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)),     ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(T, ACC)  ... </k>
    33	
    34	  // ==== heap-object arguments/receivers =====================================
    35	  // Builtins and type calls READ structure — deref the first two arg positions
    36	  // (covers len/sum/all/any/max/min/sorted/list/set + zip's pair). Mutating list
    37	  // methods take the ref itself; every other method receiver is deref'd.
    38	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    39	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    40	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    41	       [priority(40)]
    42	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (A:Val, ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    43	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (A, V, REST)) ... </k>
    44	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    45	       requires notBool isRefV(A)
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    48	        => #applyK(toCall(typeV(T)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    49	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    50	       [priority(40)]
    51	
    52	  syntax Bool ::= isMutMethod(String) [function, total]
    53	  rule isMutMethod(M:String)
    54	    => M ==String "append" orBool M ==String "sort" orBool M ==String "extend"
    55	       orBool M ==String "insert" orBool M ==String "pop" orBool M ==String "remove"
    56	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), M:String)), ACC:Vals)
    57	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(V, M)), ACC) ... </k>
    58	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    59	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M)
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	  // non-mutating methods READ their heap-object arguments too (join's list);
    62	  // mutators keep refs (append of a list into a list-of-lists stays aliased)
    63	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    64	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ, M)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    65	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    66	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M) andBool notBool isRefV(OBJ)
    67	       [priority(40)]
    68	
    69	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureVal(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, DEFL:Int)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
    70	        => #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
    71	       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
    72	       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(.Map, parent(DEFL)) ] </scopes>
    73	       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
    74	       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>
    75	
    76	  // annotated closure: the frame starts with the captured freevar cells, its
    77	  // parent is the module scope (all enclosing-local reads go through cells),
    78	  // and the cellvars' fresh cells allocate before params bind (a cellvar param
    79	  // then writes through its cell in #bindP).
    80	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureValC(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
    81	        => #allocCells(CVS) ~> #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
    82	       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
    83	       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(CM [ "$cells" <- cellsMark(CVS) ], parent(0)) ] </scopes>
    84	       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
    85	       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>
    86	
    87	  syntax KItem ::= #allocCells(ParamNames)
    88	  rule <k> #allocCells(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #allocCells((CV:String, R:ParamNames)) => #allocCells(R) ... </k>
    90	       <env> L:Int </env>
    91	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ CV <- cellRef(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    92	       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> cellV(noneV)) H </heap>
    93	       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
    94	       requires notBool N in_keys(H)
    95	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/operators.k — MPY-OPERATORS
     2	// The operator DISPATCH layer: operands evaluate by strictness (heat/cool over KResult=Val),
     3	// the cooled node hands to applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp (declared in core.k; each domain file
     4	// owns its cases — bool.k, int.k, float.k, str.k, list.k, tuple.k, set.k, dict.k).
     5	
     6	module MPY-OPERATORS
     7	  imports MPY-CORE
     8	  imports MPY-ITER
     9	
    10	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, V:Val) => applyUn(OP, V) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, R:Val) => applyBin(OP, L, R) ... </k>
    13	
    14	  // Compare's right operand sits under the CmpOp wrapper — contexts instead of attributes
    15	  context Compare(HOLE, _)
    16	  context Compare(_:Val, CmpOp(_, HOLE))
    17	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, RV:Val)) => applyCmp(OP, LV, RV) ... </k> [owise]
    18	
    19	  rule applyCmp("is",     V:Val, noneV) => V ==K noneV
    20	  rule applyCmp("is not", V:Val, noneV) => notBool (V ==K noneV)
    21	
    22	  // ==== operand deref: heap objects combine/compare by STRUCTURE ============
    23	  // (Python: list == is structural; identity only via `is`.) priority(40)
    24	  // preempts the generic dispatch so applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp never see a ref.
    25	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int), R:Expr) => BinOp(OP, V, R) ... </k>
    26	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    27	       [priority(40)]
    28	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, ref(H:Int)) => BinOp(OP, L, V) ... </k>
    29	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    30	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // the left operand of `in`/`not in` is an ELEMENT (compares by ==K) — never deref'd
    34	  rule <k> Compare(ref(H:Int), CmpOp(OP:String, R:Expr)) => Compare(V, CmpOp(OP, R)) ... </k>
    35	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    36	       requires OP =/=String "in" andBool OP =/=String "not in"
    37	       [priority(40)]
    38	  rule <k> Compare(L:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int))) => Compare(L, CmpOp(OP, V)) ... </k>
    39	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    40	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    41	        orBool OP ==String "in" orBool OP ==String "not in"
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	
    44	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int)) => UnaryOp(OP, V) ... </k>
    45	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/int.k — MPY-INT
     2	// Int cases of the operator dispatch; Python // and % are floored (pyMod).
     3	
     4	module MPY-INT
     5	  imports MPY-CORE
     6	
     7	  rule applyUn("-", I:Int) => 0 -Int I
     8	
     9	  rule applyBin("+",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 +Int I2
    10	  // Bool participates in int arithmetic (x += (a == b))
    11	  rule applyBin("+",  I:Int, B:Bool) => I +Int #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi
    12	  rule applyBin("+",  B:Bool, I:Int) => #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi +Int I
    13	  rule applyBin("-",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 -Int I2
    14	  rule applyBin("*",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 *Int I2
    15	  rule applyBin("%",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => pyMod(I1, I2)
    16	  rule applyBin("//", I1:Int, I2:Int) => (I1 -Int pyMod(I1, I2)) /Int I2
    17	  rule applyBin("**", I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 ^Int I2 requires I2 >=Int 0
    18	
    19	  syntax Int ::= pyMod(Int, Int) [function]
    20	  rule pyMod(I1:Int, I2:Int) => ((I1 %Int I2) +Int I2) %Int I2
    21	
    22	  rule applyCmp("<",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <Int  I2
    23	  rule applyCmp("<=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <=Int I2
    24	  rule applyCmp(">",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >Int  I2
    25	  rule applyCmp(">=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >=Int I2
    26	  rule applyCmp("==", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 ==Int I2
    27	  rule applyCmp("!=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 =/=Int I2
    28	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/float.k — MPY-FLOAT
     2	//
     3	// Minimal, TRUSTED float support. K/Haskell (kprove) has no usable symbolic IEEE-754 theory and
     4	// no Int2Float hook, so a float value stays an OPAQUE proof-domain primitive: `intFloatDiv(I, F)`
     5	// (the Python true division I / F) is `[no-evaluators]` for kprove — it never reduces on symbolic
     6	// input, and the proof verifies only the STRUCTURE (the result is the exact term the program
     7	// builds). The `[concrete]` rule evaluates it for krun (llvm HAS the Int2Float / /Float hooks), so
     8	// smoke tests run the real float value.
     9	//
    10	// Only the pieces needed so far: Float as a Val, the float literal, and Int / float true division
    11	// (the `a * h / 2.0` idiom). More float ops (float +/-/*, comparison) are added as float problems
    12	// need them — kept minimal + sound.

     1	// reference/src/semantics/dict.k — MPY-DICT
     2	//
     3	// Minimal dict support. A dict value is `dictV(KS, VS)`: PARALLEL insertion-ordered key/value
     4	// ValSeqs (Python dict order; keys distinct; re-inserting a key updates its value in place, keeping
     5	// the original position). Concrete for krun (the ordered build + `.keys()` are the real ops); a proof
     6	// over a SYMBOLIC dict passes `dictV(KS, WS)` with a symbolic key sequence KS and reads
     7	// `d.keys() = list(KS)`, then keeps each key opaque problem-locally.
     8	//
     9	// Only the pieces needed so far: a dict VALUE (so `{}` inside a mixed list evaluates and
    10	// `isinstance(x, int)` rejects it), the `{k: v, ...}` literal, and `.keys()`. More dict ops (subscript
    11	// / `.get()` / `.values()` / dict `==`) are added as dict problems need them — kept minimal + additive.
    12	
    13	module MPY-DICT
    14	  imports MPY-CORE
    15	  imports MPY-ITER
    16	  imports MPY-METHODS
    17	  imports MPY-LIST
    18	
    19	  // dict as PARALLEL ordered key/value ValSeqs (same length; keys distinct).
    20	  syntax Val ::= dictV(ValSeq, ValSeq)
    21	
    22	  // ==== DictExpr: {k: v, ...} literal. Eval each key then value, left to right, insert-with-dedup.
    23	  syntax KItem ::= #dictAcc(Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    24	                 | #dictKey(Expr, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    25	                 | #dictVal(Val, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    26	  rule <k> DictExpr(ES:Entries) => #dictAcc(ES, .ValSeq, .ValSeq) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #dictAcc(.Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq) => dictV(KS, VS) ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #dictAcc((Entry(K:Expr, V:Expr), REST:Entries), KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    29	        => K ~> #dictKey(V, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dictKey(V:Expr, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    31	        => V ~> #dictVal(KV, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    32	  rule <k> VV:Val ~> #dictVal(KV:Val, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    33	        => #dictAcc(REST, dPutK(KS, KV), dPutV(KS, VS, KV, VV)) ... </k>
    34	
    35	  // insert-with-dedup helpers (concrete Val key equality via ==K). [total] so buildFold over a dict is
    36	  // total (its #Ceil is #Top) — needed when a symbolic proof carries a built dict as a config value.
    37	  syntax Bool ::= dHasKey(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    38	  rule dHasKey(.ValSeq, _:Val)                => false
    39	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => true          requires A ==K K
    40	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), K:Val) => dHasKey(R, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
    41	
    42	  // dPutK: KS unchanged if K already present, else append K (keep-first-position).
    43	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutK(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    44	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => KS                                  requires dHasKey(KS, K)
    45	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => valSeqConcat(KS, vCons(K, .ValSeq)) requires notBool dHasKey(KS, K)
    46	
    47	  // dPutV: parallel to KS — set the value at K's position if present, else append V at the end. The
    48	  // [owise] catch-all covers the degenerate mismatched-length case (never reached for a well-formed dict).
    49	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutV(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val, Val) [function, total]
    50	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)  => vCons(V, VR)
    51	       requires A ==K K
    52	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(B, dPutV(KR, VR, K, V))
    53	       requires notBool (A ==K K)
    54	  rule dPutV(_KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq, _K:Val, V:Val) => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq)) [owise]
    55	
    56	  // ==== dict methods ========================================================
    57	  // d.keys() -> a FRESH list object of the ordered keys (k-cell: it allocates).
    58	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(dictV(KS:ValSeq, _:ValSeq), "keys")), .Vals)
    59	        => #alloc(list(KS)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	
    62	  // ==== dict subscript READ: d[k] (assoc lookup; KeyError is out of subset) ==
    63	  rule applyIndexD(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KS, VS, K)
    64	  syntax Val ::= applyIndexD(Val, Val) [function]
    65	  rule <k> Subscript(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => applyIndexD(dictV(KS, VS), K) ... </k>
    66	       [priority(45)]
    67	
    68	  // ==== dict subscript-assign: d[k] = v (insert/update in place) =============
    69	  // Only for a LOCAL dict variable X (the current scope holds it). Reuses dPutK/dPutV.
    70	  syntax Val ::= dictSet(Val, Val, Val) [function]
    71	  rule dictSet(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => dictV(dPutK(KS, K), dPutV(KS, VS, K, V))
    72	
    73	  // RHS evaluates first (Assign strictness), then the key. Dispatch on the scope
    74	  // value: a bare dict updates in the scope (dicts stay values); a ref (a heap
    75	  // list — or a heap dict later) writes the heap in place.
    76	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetK(String, Val)

    78	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    79	       <env> L:Int </env>
    80	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- dictSet({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ], _) ... </scopes>
    81	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool notBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    82	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => #dsetV({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ... </k>
    83	       <env> L:Int </env>
    84	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    85	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    86	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetV(Val, Val, Val)
    87	  rule <k> #dsetV(ref(H:Int), I:Int, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    88	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => setVSAt(VS, normIdxD(I, vsLen(VS)), VV)) ... </heap>
    89	  // negative-index normalization local to the write (subscript.k's is not imported here)
    90	  syntax Int ::= normIdxD(Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    92	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    93	
    94	  // ==== dict == (order-insensitive: same size + same key->value pairs) =======
    95	  rule applyCmp("==", dictV(KS1:ValSeq, VS1:ValSeq), dictV(KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq))
    96	    => (vsLen(KS1) ==Int vsLen(KS2)) andBool dSubset(KS1, VS1, KS2, VS2)
    97	  syntax Bool ::= dSubset(ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    98	  rule dSubset(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:ValSeq, _:ValSeq) => true
    99	  rule dSubset(vCons(K:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(V:Val, VR:ValSeq), KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq)
   100	    => dHasKey(KS2, K) andBool (dGet(KS2, VS2, K) ==K V) andBool dSubset(KR, VR, KS2, VS2)
   101	  syntax Val ::= dGet(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val) [function]
   102	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => B                requires A ==K K
   103	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KR, VR, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
   104	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/sort.k — MPY-SORT
     2	// Trusted sorted(): sorted(list) as an opaque ascending permutation `sortVS` — opaque symbolic
     3	// for kprove (a trusted primitive, correctness/ordering proved in Lean / notes/sort-probe),
     4	// and a concrete insertion sort for krun. Wrappers verify the logic AROUND the sort (index /
     5	// slice / filter / dedup); indexing an opaque sortVS(VS) carries through as an opaque term, so
     6	// no ordering lemma is needed in K — the trust (sortVS = real sorted) is discharged by each
     7	// problem's differential test. Only int lists (compared by projectIntTotal); keyed / string
     8	// sorts are separate. Fires only via the "sorted" builtin, so inert for non-sorting programs.
     9	
    10	module MPY-SORT
    11	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    12	  imports MPY-SUBSCRIPT
    13	
    14	  // sortVS(VS): the ascending sort of the Val list VS. Opaque for symbolic VS (no-evaluators);
    15	  // concrete insertion sort for krun.
    16	  // Concrete sort matches Int-sorted elements directly (an int Val IS an Int); projectIntTotal
    17	  // (lemmas-only) is not available in the semantics. Int and str lists.
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= sortVS(ValSeq) [function, total, symbol(sortVS), no-evaluators]
    19	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVS(Int, ValSeq) [function]
    20	  rule sortVS(.ValSeq)                => .ValSeq          [concrete]
    21	  rule sortVS(vCons(X:Int, R:ValSeq)) => insVS(X, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
    22	  rule insVS(X:Int, .ValSeq)                => vCons(X, .ValSeq) [concrete]
    23	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(X, vCons(Y, R)) requires X <=Int Y [concrete]
    24	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(Y, insVS(X, R)) requires X  >Int Y [concrete]
    25	  // str elements insert by the shared lexicographic strLt (methods.k)
    26	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVSs(IntSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    27	  rule sortVS(vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => insVSs(CS, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
    28	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, .ValSeq) => vCons(str(A), .ValSeq) [concrete]
    29	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(A), vCons(str(B), R))
    30	       requires strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B [concrete]
    31	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(B), insVSs(A, R))
    32	       requires notBool (strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B) [concrete]
    33	
    34	  // sorted(list) constructs a NEW object: k-cell pre-dispatch (beats the [owise]
    35	  // applyBuiltin routing in call.k) so the result allocates.
    36	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), .Vals))
    37	        => #alloc(list(sortVS(VS))) ... </k>
    38	
    39	  // mutator: xs.sort() — the in-place heap write over the same trusted sortVS
    40	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "sort")), .Vals) => noneV ... </k>
    41	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => sortVS(VS)) ... </heap>
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	
    44	  // ==== keyed / reversed sorted() (WP2) =====================================
    45	  // sortKeyVS(VS, KV): the stable ascending sort of VS by the key value KV
    46	  // (a closure/builtin/type — anything callable). OPAQUE here; the concrete
    47	  // leg (MPY-CONCRETE, llvm only) computes keys by REAL calls and stable-
    48	  // inserts, at priority(40) over these.
    49	  syntax ValSeq ::= sortKeyVS(ValSeq, Val) [function, total, symbol(sortKeyVS), no-evaluators]
    50	
    51	  syntax ValSeq ::= revVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    52	                  | revVSAcc(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    53	  rule revVS(S:ValSeq) => revVSAcc(S, .ValSeq)
    54	  rule revVSAcc(.ValSeq, A:ValSeq) => A
    55	  rule revVSAcc(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), A:ValSeq) => revVSAcc(R, vCons(V, A))
    56	
    57	  syntax ValSeq ::= condRev(ValSeq, Bool) [function, total]
    58	  rule condRev(S:ValSeq, false) => S
    59	  rule condRev(S:ValSeq, true)  => revVS(S)
    60	
    61	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), .Vals))
    62	        => #alloc(list(sortKeyVS(VS, KV))) ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    64	        => #alloc(list(condRev(sortKeyVS(VS, KV), RB))) ... </k>
    65	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    66	        => #alloc(list(condRev(sortVS(VS), RB))) ... </k>
    67	
    68	  // Indexing the opaque sorted list: `valSeqAt(sortVS(VS), I)` is DEFINED because valSeqAt is
    69	  // [total] (subscript.k) — it stays an abstract total value for a symbolic sort and reduces
    70	  // over the concrete sort for krun. No separate sortedAt indirection is needed; wrappers write
    71	  // their postcondition directly as valSeqAt(sortVS(VS), …).
    72	endmodule

     9	
    10	  rule applyCmp("==", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 ==Bool B2
    11	  rule applyCmp("!=", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 =/=Bool B2
    12	
    13	  // ==== BoolOp: short-circuit, value-returning and / or =====================
    14	  // the node is its own accumulator: heat the HEAD element only, then either return it
    15	  // (short-circuit) or drop it and continue
    16	  context BoolOp(_, (HOLE:Expr, _:Exprs))
    17	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (V:Val, .Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    18	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    19	       requires truthy(V)
    20	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    21	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    22	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    23	       requires truthy(V)
    24	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    25	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    26	
    27	  // ==== heap-object head: decide truthiness THROUGH the heap, never rewrite the
    28	  // operand — and/or return the OBJECT itself (Python identity), not its structure
    29	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (ref(H:Int), .Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    30	       [priority(40)]
    31	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       requires truthy(V)
    34	       [priority(40)]
    35	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    36	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    37	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    38	       [priority(40)]
    39	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    40	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    41	       requires truthy(V)
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    44	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    45	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	endmodule
--- reference-semantics/semantics/comprehension.k ---
     1	// reference/src/semantics/comprehension.k — MPY-COMPREHENSION
     2	
     3	module MPY-COMPREHENSION
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     6	  imports MPY-LIST
     7	  imports MPY-CONTROLS
     8	  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
     9	
    10	  // A comprehension is pure syntactic sugar
    11	  rule ListComp(ELT:Expr, Gs:CompFors) => Call(closureExpr(.ParamNames, compBody(Gs, ELT)), .Exprs)
    12	  rule GenExp(ELT:Expr, Gs:CompFors)   => Call(closureExpr(.ParamNames, compBody(Gs, ELT)), .Exprs)
    13	
    14	  syntax Stmts ::= compBody(CompFors, Expr) [macro]
    15	  rule compBody(Gs:CompFors, ELT:Expr)
    16	    => Assign(Name("$acc"), ListExpr(.Exprs)) compNest(Gs, ELT) Return(Name("$acc"))
    17	
    18	  syntax Stmt ::= compNest(CompFors, Expr) [macro-rec]
    19	  rule compNest(.CompFors, ELT:Expr)
    20	    => Assign(Name("$acc"), BinOp("+", Name("$acc"), ListExpr(ELT)))
    21	  rule compNest((CompFor(T:Expr, ITER:Expr, Fs:Exprs) GRest:CompFors), ELT:Expr)
    22	    => For(T, ITER, If(compGuard(Fs), compNest(GRest, ELT), .Stmts))
    23	
    24	  syntax Expr ::= compGuard(Exprs) [macro]
    25	  rule compGuard(.Exprs)             => Bool(true)
    26	  rule compGuard((F:Expr, Fs:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (F, Fs))
    27	endmodule
--- reference-semantics/semantics/concrete.k ---
     1	// reference/src/semantics/concrete.k — MPY-CONCRETE
     2	// Concrete-execution-only rules, visible ONLY to the llvm build (run.sh kompiles
     3	// MPY-CONCRETE; verification builds import MPY and never see these). Rationale:
     4	// a k-cell rule matching value constructors NARROWS abstract Vals in the haskell
     5	// backend ([concrete] is not respected on rewrite rules) — probed on
     6	// 26-remove-duplicates, where element compares branched into deepEqVS.
     7	
     8	module MPY-CONCRETE
     9	  imports MPY
    10	
    11	  // deep equality for list compares whose elements are heap objects
    12	  // (list-of-lists): Python == is structural at every depth.
    13	  rule <k> Compare(list(A:ValSeq), CmpOp("==", list(B:ValSeq))) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP) ... </k>
    14	       <heap> HP:Map </heap>
    15	       requires hasRefVS(A) orBool hasRefVS(B)
    16	  rule <k> Compare(list(A:ValSeq), CmpOp("!=", list(B:ValSeq))) => notBool deepEqVS(A, B, HP) ... </k>
    17	       <heap> HP:Map </heap>
    18	       requires hasRefVS(A) orBool hasRefVS(B)
    19	
    20	  // ==== keyed sort, concrete leg ============================================
    21	  // Computes each key by a REAL call through the uniform #callee machinery
    22	  // (closures, len, type objects all work), stable-inserts on the key, and
    23	  // allocates the result. priority(40) beats sort.k's opaque rules, so krun
    24	  // runs this and proofs (which never see MPY-CONCRETE) keep sortKeyVS.
    25	  syntax Val ::= kvP(Val, Val)
    26	  syntax KItem ::= #ksort(ValSeq, Val, ValSeq, Bool)
    27	                 | #ksIns(Val, ValSeq, Val, ValSeq, Bool)
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), .Vals))
    29	        => #ksort(VS, KV, .ValSeq, false) ... </k>
    30	       [priority(40)]
    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    32	        => #ksort(VS, KV, .ValSeq, RB) ... </k>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	  rule <k> #ksort(.ValSeq, _:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    35	        => #alloc(list(condRev(unpairVS(ACC), RB))) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> #ksort(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), KV:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    37	        => KV ~> #callee((V, .Exprs)) ~> #ksIns(V, R, KV, ACC, RB) ... </k>
    38	  rule <k> K:Val ~> #ksIns(V:Val, R:ValSeq, KV:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    39	        => #ksort(R, KV, insPair(ACC, K, V), RB) ... </k>
    40	       requires notBool isKwV(K)
    41	
    42	  syntax ValSeq ::= insPair(ValSeq, Val, Val) [function]
    43	  rule insPair(.ValSeq, K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(kvP(K, V), .ValSeq)
    44	  rule insPair(vCons(kvP(K2:Val, V2:Val), R:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)
    45	    => vCons(kvP(K, V), vCons(kvP(K2, V2), R))
    46	       requires kLt(K, K2)
    47	  rule insPair(vCons(kvP(K2:Val, V2:Val), R:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)
    48	    => vCons(kvP(K2, V2), insPair(R, K, V))
    49	       requires notBool kLt(K, K2)
    50	
    51	  syntax Bool ::= kLt(Val, Val) [function]
    52	  rule kLt(I1:Int, I2:Int)             => I1 <Int I2
    53	  rule kLt(F1:Float, F2:Float)         => F1 <Float F2
    54	  rule kLt(str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)
    55	
    56	  syntax ValSeq ::= unpairVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    57	  rule unpairVS(.ValSeq) => .ValSeq
    58	  rule unpairVS(vCons(kvP(_:Val, V:Val), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(V, unpairVS(R))
    59	  rule unpairVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(V, unpairVS(R)) [owise]
    60	endmodule
--- reference-semantics/semantics/iter.k ---
     1	// reference/src/semantics/iter.k — MPY-ITER
     2	// The iterator protocol, DECLARATION ONLY. Each iterable's #iterNext case lives in that
     3	// iterable's own module (list/tuple/str in their modules, rangeObj in range.k, zip in
     4	// builtins.k). Consumers (the for-loop, `x in _`, sum/all/any/max/min) import this.
     5	
     6	module MPY-ITER
     7	  imports MPY-CORE
     8	  syntax KItem ::= #iterNext(Iterable) | "#iterDone" | #iterYield(Val, Iterable)
     9	endmodule
--- reference-semantics/semantics/list.k ---
     1	// reference/src/semantics/list.k — MPY-LIST
     2	
     3	module MPY-LIST
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     7	
     8	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's list case) =======================
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, list(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== ListExpr: [...] literal -> a fresh heap object =======================
    13	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toList"
    14	  rule <k> ListExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toList) ... </k>
    15	  rule <k> #applyK(toList, ACC:Vals) => #alloc(list(vals2valSeq(ACC))) ... </k>
    16	
    17	  // ==== list ops: + / == / != ===============================================
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= valSeqConcat(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    19	  rule valSeqConcat(.ValSeq, T:ValSeq)                => T
    20	  rule valSeqConcat(vCons(V:Val, S:ValSeq), T:ValSeq) => vCons(V, valSeqConcat(S, T))
    21	
    22	  // list + list constructs a NEW object (k-cell — it allocates; operands land here
    23	  // already deref'd). priority(45) beats the generic BinOp dispatch.
    24	  rule <k> BinOp("+", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => #alloc(list(valSeqConcat(A, B))) ... </k>
    25	       [priority(45)]
    26	
    27	  rule applyCmp("==", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    28	  rule applyCmp("!=", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    29	
    30	  // ==== deep equality when elements are heap objects (list-of-lists) ========
    31	  // Python == is structural at every depth. Fires ONLY when a ref is present
    32	  // (the guard decides on concrete seqs); the plain ==K path above is unchanged.
    33	  syntax Bool ::= hasRefVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    34	  rule hasRefVS(.ValSeq)                => false
    35	  rule hasRefVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => isRefV(V) orBool hasRefVS(R)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= deepEqVS(ValSeq, ValSeq, Map) [function]
    38	                | deepEqV(Val, Val, Map)        [function]
    39	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:Map)                   => true
    40	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), _:Map)    => false
    41	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), .ValSeq, _:Map)    => false
    42	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(A:Val, As:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, Bs:ValSeq), HP:Map)
    43	    => deepEqV(A, B, HP) andBool deepEqVS(As, Bs, HP)
    44	
    45	  rule deepEqV(ref(H:Int), B:Val, HP:Map) => deepEqV({HP[H]}:>Val, B, HP)
    46	       requires H in_keys(HP)
    47	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, ref(H:Int), HP:Map) => deepEqV(A, {HP[H]}:>Val, HP)
    48	       requires notBool isRefV(A) andBool H in_keys(HP)
    49	  rule deepEqV(list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), HP:Map) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP)
    50	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, B:Val, _:Map) => A ==K B [owise]
    51	
    52	  // ==== mutator: xs.append(v) — an in-place heap write ======================
    53	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "append")), (V:Val, .Vals)) => noneV ... </k>
    54	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq))) ... </heap>
    55	       [priority(40)]
    56	
    57	  // ==== `x in list` — a <k>-cell fold over #iterNext ========================
    58	  syntax KItem ::= #memberAcc(Val, Iterable) | #memberCont(Val) | "#notB"
    59	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ... </k>
    60	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #memberAcc(V:Val, IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #memberCont(V) ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #memberCont(_V:Val) => false ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>
    64	       requires E ==K V
    65	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>
    66	       requires notBool (E ==K V)
    67	  rule <k> B:Bool ~> #notB => notBool B ... </k>
    68	endmodule
--- reference-semantics/semantics/range.k ---
     1	// reference/src/semantics/range.k — MPY-RANGE
     2	// rangeObj: the range helpers (inRange / rangeLen) + its #iterNext case. rangeObj itself is
     3	// declared in MPY-CORE's Iterable union; this module owns its behavior.
     4	
     5	module MPY-RANGE
     6	  imports MPY-CORE
     7	  imports MPY-ITER
     8	
     9	  syntax Bool ::= inRange(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
    10	  rule inRange(I:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int) => (ST >Int 0 andBool I <Int HI) orBool (ST <Int 0 andBool I >Int HI)
    11	
    12	  syntax Int ::= rangeLen(Int, Int, Int) [function]
    13	  rule rangeLen(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int) => (HI -Int LO +Int ST -Int 1) /Int ST
    14	       requires ST >Int 0 andBool HI >Int LO
    15	  rule rangeLen(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int) => (LO -Int HI -Int ST -Int 1) /Int (0 -Int ST)
    16	       requires ST <Int 0 andBool HI <Int LO
    17	  rule rangeLen(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int) => 0
    18	       requires (ST >Int 0 andBool HI <=Int LO) orBool (ST <Int 0 andBool HI >=Int LO)
    19	
    20	  rule <k> #iterNext(rangeObj(I:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int))
    21	        => #iterYield(I, rangeObj(I +Int ST, HI, ST)) ... </k>
    22	       requires inRange(I, HI, ST)
    23	  rule <k> #iterNext(rangeObj(I:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int)) => #iterDone ... </k>
    24	       requires notBool inRange(I, HI, ST)
    25	endmodule
--- reference-semantics/semantics/set.k ---
     1	// reference/src/semantics/set.k — MPY-SET
     2	
     3	module MPY-SET
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // a set value, carried as its distinct codes in first-seen order (order is irrelevant
     7	  // to membership/cardinality — the two observations sets support here).
     8	  syntax Val ::= setV(IntSeq)
     9	
    10	  // membership of a code in the accumulated distinct-code sequence
    11	  syntax Bool ::= codeIn(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
    12	  rule codeIn(_:Int, .IntSeq)                => false
    13	  rule codeIn(C:Int, iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq)) => C ==Int H orBool codeIn(C, T)
    14	
    15	  // the distinct codes of CS (insert-if-absent fold, first-seen order)
    16	  syntax IntSeq ::= dedupCodes(IntSeq)         [function, total]
    17	                  | dedupFrom(IntSeq, IntSeq)  [function, total]
    18	  rule dedupCodes(CS:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(CS, .IntSeq)
    19	  rule dedupFrom(.IntSeq, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
    20	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, ACC)
    21	       requires codeIn(C, ACC)
    22	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, snocCode(ACC, C))
    23	       requires notBool codeIn(C, ACC)
    24	
    25	  syntax IntSeq ::= snocCode(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
    26	  rule snocCode(.IntSeq, C:Int)                => iCons(C, .IntSeq)
    27	  rule snocCode(iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq), C:Int) => iCons(H, snocCode(T, C))
    28	
    29	  // ==== set equality: two sets are equal iff mutually subsuming ==============
    30	  // subsetCodes(A, B) — every code of A occurs in B (duplicates in A are harmless).
    31	  syntax Bool ::= subsetCodes(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    32	  rule subsetCodes(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)                => true
    33	  rule subsetCodes(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), B:IntSeq) => codeIn(C, B) andBool subsetCodes(S, B)
    34	
    35	  syntax Bool ::= sameSet(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    36	  rule sameSet(A:IntSeq, B:IntSeq) => subsetCodes(A, B) andBool subsetCodes(B, A)
    37	
    38	  // set == set  (the only comparison sets support here)
    39	  rule applyCmp("==", setV(A:IntSeq), setV(B:IntSeq)) => sameSet(A, B)
    40	endmodule
--- reference-semantics/semantics/str.k ---
     1	// reference/src/semantics/str.k — MPY-STR
     2	
     3	module MPY-STR
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	
     7	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's str case; yields 1-char strings) ==
     8	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(.IntSeq))                 => #iterDone ... </k>
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)))
    10	        => #iterYield(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), str(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== str literal (ASCII-only) ============================================
    13	  syntax IntSeq ::= strToCodes(String) [function]
    14	  rule <k> Str(S:String) => str(strToCodes(S)) ... </k>
    15	  rule strToCodes("") => .IntSeq
    16	  rule strToCodes(S:String) => iCons(ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)), strToCodes(substrString(S, 1, lengthString(S))))
    17	    requires S =/=String "" andBool ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)) <Int 128
    18	
    19	  // ==== operators: + / == / != / in =========================================
    20	  syntax IntSeq ::= seqConcat(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    21	  rule seqConcat(.IntSeq, T:IntSeq)                => T
    22	  rule seqConcat(iCons(I:Int, S:IntSeq), T:IntSeq) => iCons(I, seqConcat(S, T))
    23	
    24	  rule applyBin("+",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => str(seqConcat(A, B))
    25	  rule applyCmp("==", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => A ==K B
    26	  rule applyCmp("!=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    27	
    28	  // substring membership: `P in X` iff the code-seq P occurs contiguously in X
    29	  rule applyCmp("in",     str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, X)
    30	  rule applyCmp("not in", str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => notBool strContains(P, X)
    31	
    32	  syntax Bool ::= strPrefix(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    33	  rule strPrefix(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)               => true
    34	  rule strPrefix(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    35	  rule strPrefix(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => A ==Int B andBool strPrefix(As, Bs)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= strContains(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    38	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, X:IntSeq) => true  requires strPrefix(P, X)
    39	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, .IntSeq)  => false requires notBool strPrefix(P, .IntSeq)
    40	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, iCons(C:Int, Xs:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, Xs)
    41	       requires notBool strPrefix(P, iCons(C, Xs))
    42	
    43	  // ==== lexicographic order: < / <= / > / >= by code point (= Python str order on the code
    44	  // model). strLt reduces on GROUND code-seqs (krun) but is inert/OPAQUE on symbolic ones
    45	  // (a proof's codesProj(V) is an abstract IntSeq — no constructor rule matches), so a symbolic
    46	  // str `<` stays a trusted opaque term the way sortVS / intFloatDiv do. Additive: fires only on
    47	  // str </<=/>/>= comparisons.
    48	  syntax Bool ::= strLt(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    49	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, .IntSeq)                => false
    50	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq)) => true
    51	  rule strLt(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    52	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => true          requires A  <Int B
    53	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => false         requires A  >Int B
    54	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => strLt(As, Bs) requires A ==Int B
    55	
    56	  rule applyCmp("<",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)
    57	  rule applyCmp(">",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(B, A)
    58	  rule applyCmp("<=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(B, A)
    59	  rule applyCmp(">=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(A, B)
    60	endmodule
--- reference-semantics/semantics/tuple.k ---
     1	// reference/src/semantics/tuple.k — MPY-TUPLE
     2	
     3	module MPY-TUPLE
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-LIST
     7	  imports MPY-METHODS
     8	
     9	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's tuple case) ======================
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(tuple(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    11	  rule <k> #iterNext(tuple(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, tuple(R)) ... </k>
    12	
    13	  // ==== TupleExpr: tuple(ValSeq) literal + == != ===========================
    14	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toTuple"
    15	  rule <k> TupleExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toTuple) ... </k>
    16	  rule <k> #applyK(toTuple, ACC:Vals) => tuple(vals2valSeq(ACC)) ... </k>
    17

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bounded semantic inspection of every structured generation-trace event."""

import collections
import hashlib
import json
import pathlib


trace_files = sorted(
    pathlib.Path("/generation-evidence/codex-trace").rglob("*.jsonl")
)
calls = []
messages = []
counts = collections.Counter()

for path in trace_files:
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        for line_number, line in enumerate(stream, 1):
            event = json.loads(line)
            payload = event.get("payload")
            payload_type = payload.get("type") if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
            counts[str(payload_type)] += 1
            if payload_type == "agent_message":
                messages.append(
                    (
                        line_number,
                        payload.get("phase"),
                        payload.get("message", ""),
                    )
                )
            if payload_type in {"function_call", "custom_tool_call"}:
                name = payload.get("name")
                argument = payload.get("arguments", payload.get("input", ""))
                if not isinstance(argument, str):
                    argument = json.dumps(argument, sort_keys=True)
                calls.append(
                    (
                        line_number,
                        name,
                        len(argument),
                        hashlib.sha256(argument.encode()).hexdigest(),
                        argument[:300].replace("\n", "\\n"),
                    )
                )

print("trace_files=", [str(path) for path in trace_files])
print("payload_counts=", dict(sorted(counts.items())))
print("agent_message_count=", len(messages))
for line_number, phase, message in messages:
    print(f"AGENT_MESSAGE line={line_number} phase={phase}: {message}")
print("tool_call_count=", len(calls))
for line_number, name, size, digest, preview in calls:
    print(
        f"TOOL_CALL line={line_number} name={name} bytes={size} "
        f"sha256={digest} preview={preview}"
    )

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /audit-output/REVIEW.md
+# Independent adversarial audit: 139-special-factorial
+
+## Outcome
+
+The candidate contains a legitimate partial-correctness proof of the submitted
+program for the full source-contract domain: every K integer `N >= 1`. I rebuilt
+both definitions from source, proved the complete target module with a fresh
+Haskell definition, mechanically pinned the entry claim to the trusted
+regeneration of `solution.mpy`, audited every source declaration and rule, and
+rejected a fresh false result mutation. No candidate-provided compiled
+definition, log, trace, or proof report was used as proof authority.
+
+The only assumptions are the normal toolchain trust boundary, the supplied MPY
+semantics for the small reachable integer/control fragment, the trusted
+translator, and a transparent mathematical induction from the accumulator
+recurrence to the product of factorials. None is a proof-local oracle or an
+execution bypass.
+
+## 1. Input and provenance integrity
+
+### Launcher record and campaign
+
+`/audit-input.json` declares:
+
+- `record_layout = pipeline-v3`
+- `semantics_mode = SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`
+- problem `139-special-factorial`
+- condition `kit-semantics`
+
+I read every pipeline-v3 record required by the prompt: `/run.json`,
+`/task.json`, `/generation-result.json`,
+`/generation-evidence/invocation.json`, `metrics.json`,
+`runtime-metrics.json`, `usage.json`, `codex-last.txt`, `codex-output.log`,
+`prompt.txt`, and the complete structured trace. The JSONL trace has 445 valid
+records: 315 response items, 127 event messages, and one each of session
+metadata, turn context, and world state. A bounded semantic extraction records
+all 16 agent messages and all 96 tool calls. These records were treated only as
+untrusted construction history.
+
+The `audit_campaign` object is exactly equal to
+`/audit-campaign-lock.json`. The lock's independently computed SHA-256 is
+`ad5dfcc006af70c4d0d2c6641f0878a6c54a266e9ad2b54cd225b2381a78d745`,
+which equals the value recorded in `/audit-input.json`.
+
+All direct recorded hashes match the mounted files, including the run, task,
+result, invocation, prompt, canonical, translator, generation logs, metrics,
+usage, and trace. Every generation-result evidence hash also matches. The
+`manifest` object embedded in `/audit-input.json` adds the synthesized `config`
+field; after removing that one launcher-added field, it exactly equals
+`/task.json`. The raw task-file hash matches its recorded hash.
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `evidence/01_provenance.py`
+- `evidence/01_provenance_corrected.log` (command exit `0`)
+- `evidence/01_trace_summary.py`
+- `evidence/01_trace_summary.log` (command exit `0`)
+- `evidence/01_provenance.log` (initial scan; its `file` utility probe was
+  unavailable, but all required checks completed and the wrapper exited `0`)
+
+### Trusted/candidate input comparison
+
+The trusted `/reference/reference-semantics` tree is present, as required for
+`SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`. A recursive no-dereference comparison against
+`/candidate/reference-semantics` exits `0`. The trees have identical entries
+and bytes; there are no missing, additional, mistyped, symlinked, or special
+entries. The candidate prompt and translator are byte-identical to
+`/reference/prompt.py` and `/reference/py2mpy.py`.
+
+The six required candidate proof artifacts are ordinary regular files:
+`solution.py`, `solution.mpy`, `verification.k`, `spec.k`, `prove.sh`, and
+`PROOF.md`. The entire candidate tree has no symlinks or special entries.
+Candidate-built `runtime-kompiled` and `verification-kompiled` were ignored.
+There is no infrastructure breach.
+
+## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks
+
+### Contract and implementation
+
+The trusted prompt defines, for a positive integer `n`, the Brazilian/special
+factorial
+
+```text
+n! * (n-1)! * ... * 1!
+```
+
+and gives `special_factorial(4) == 288`. The trusted canonical program maintains
+an ordinary factorial accumulator and multiplies it into a second accumulator
+for `i = 1..n`.
+
+The candidate uses the same recurrence in a `while` loop:
+
+```python
+factorial = factorial * i
+result = result * factorial
+i = i + 1
+```
+
+It is a different surface loop form but the same algorithm. The loop executes
+once at `n=1`, repeatedly for larger positive integers, and never executes for
+nonpositive inputs.
+
+### Trusted regeneration
+
+In `/tmp/audit-work/reconstruction`, I ran:
+
+```bash
+python3 /reference/py2mpy.py solution.py > regenerated-solution.mpy
+cmp -s solution.mpy regenerated-solution.mpy
+```
+
+Both commands exit `0`. Submitted and regenerated `.mpy` files have the same
+SHA-256,
+`0c3b214dd2e101f2b7f6c6d881c50335503145f96fbfd1858f5b130d452a78c3`.
+
+### Independent differential test
+
+`evidence/02_differential.py` independently imports the trusted canonical and
+the scratch-copied generated implementation. It checks:
+
+- out-of-domain no-iteration cases `-3, -1, 0`;
+- the positive boundary and first branch lengths `1, 2, 3`;
+- the documented example `4`;
+- fixed representatives through `50`;
+- 30 distinct positive values generated with seed `139`, up to `75`;
+- an independent `math.prod(math.factorial(...))` oracle on all positive cases.
+
+The 38-input run reports `mismatch_count=0`, `n=4 -> 288`, `n=1 -> 1`, and
+`n=2 -> 2`. Exact command and exit:
+
+```bash
+/audit-output/evidence/02_program_fidelity.sh
+# exit 0
+```
+
+Evidence: `evidence/02_program_fidelity.sh` and
+`evidence/02_program_fidelity.log`.
+
+## 3. Clean proof reconstruction
+
+I copied only source artifacts into `/tmp/audit-work/reconstruction`, copied
+the semantics from the trusted `/reference` mount, and created new output
+directories named `audit-runtime-kompiled` and
+`audit-verification-kompiled`. No candidate cache or compiled definition was
+copied or referenced. The independently observed tool version is K v7.1.293.
+
+### Fresh concrete definition
+
+Commands:
+
+```bash
+kompile --backend llvm reference-semantics/semantics.k \
+  --main-module MPY-KRUN \
+  --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
+  --output-definition audit-runtime-kompiled
+
+krun regenerated-smoke.mpy --definition audit-runtime-kompiled
+```
+
+The trusted translator also reproduced `smoke.mpy` byte-for-byte before this
+run. The LLVM build exits `0`. The concrete run consumes assertions for
+`N=1..6`, exits `0`, and ends with `.K`, `NoExc`, empty stack, `noRet`, and
+exit code `0`.
+
+### Fresh proof definition and every positive claim
+
+Commands:
+
+```bash
+kompile --backend haskell verification.k \
+  --main-module VERIFICATION \
+  --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
+  --output-definition audit-verification-kompiled
+
+kprove spec.k \
+  --definition audit-verification-kompiled \
+  --spec-module SPEC
+
+kprove summary-test.k \
+  --definition audit-verification-kompiled \
+  --spec-module SUMMARY-TEST
+```
+
+The Haskell build exits `0`. The complete `SPEC` command proves both
+`loop-invariant` and `special-factorial`; it prints `#Top` and exits `0`.
+The supporting module's twelve positive ground claims for both summary
+functions at `N=1..6` also print `#Top` and exit `0`. Their
+`WarnTrivialClaim` messages mean the ground functions simplified before a
+reachability step; they are not failures.
+
+The compiler warnings concern fixed, unused supplied-semantics helpers and are
+accounted for in Stage 5. None occurs in candidate proof-local rules or on the
+reachable program path.
+
+Evidence: `evidence/03_reconstruct.sh` and
+`evidence/03_reconstruct.log` (wrapper exit `0`, with exact outputs and
+individual exit statuses).
+
+## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning
+
+### Claims in plain language
+
+`SPEC.loop-invariant` starts at the actual recurring internal loop head
+`#while(...)`. Its precondition is:
+
+```text
+N >= 1, 1 <= I <= N + 1
+```
+
+with current locals `n=N`, `i=I`, `factorial=F`, and `result=R`. It executes
+the exact three-statement source loop, consumes only that loop, preserves the
+continuation and all framed cells, and finishes with:
+
+```text
+i         = N + 1
+factorial = factorialAfter(I, N, F)
+result    = productAfter(I, N, F, R)
+```
+
+`SPEC.special-factorial` starts from the standard empty module scope, trusted
+builtins scope, empty heap and stack, normal return/exception state, and
+`N >= 1`. It loads the exact translated function, calls its resulting binding
+with `N`, and reaches:
+
+```text
+productAfter(1, N, 1, 1)
+```
+
+The final module binding remains present; the callee frame is deallocated; the
+environment, allocator, heap, stack, return state, exception state, and exit
+code are restored or constrained to their intended values. The result is not a
+right-only free variable, tautology, or implication.
+
+### Mechanical constructor-level program identity
+
+`evidence/04_constructor_compare.py` removes only whitespace and compares the
+trusted-regenerated complete `Module(FuncDef(...))` against the `#loadAll`
+argument in the entry claim. It finds exactly one exact occurrence. It also
+checks the exact `special_factorial` call, positive unbounded integer
+precondition, and result recurrence. The check exits `0`.
+
+Thus the claim mechanically pins the submitted function name, parameter,
+binding, initializations, guard, all three ordered body assignments, and
+return. No typing import or other normalization is omitted.
+
+### Satisfiable states and concrete substitutions
+
+`evidence/04_witnesses.k` supplies two fresh ground claims:
+
+- loop witness `N=4, I=1, F=1, R=1, L=1`, ending at
+  `factorial=24`, `result=288`, `i=5`;
+- full entry witness `N=4`, returning the independent ground integer `288`
+  rather than a symbolic summary.
+
+Together they exhibit realizable states for both candidate preconditions. The
+module prints `#Top` and exits `0`. Both trusted canonical Python and candidate
+Python also return `288`. Ground summary proofs additionally establish:
+
+```text
+N=1 -> 1
+N=2 -> 2
+N=3 -> 12
+N=4 -> 288
+N=5 -> 34560
+N=6 -> 24883200
+```
+
+The recurrence has the intended mathematical meaning. At loop head `I`, let
+`F=(I-1)!` and `R=product(k!, 1 <= k < I)`, with the empty product equal to
+one. The first assignment makes `F'=F*I=I!`; the second makes
+`R'=R*F'=product(k!, 1 <= k <= I)`; the last makes `I'=I+1`. At exit
+`I=N+1`, so `R=N!*(N-1)!*...*1!`. This is a direct induction over the same
+recurrence, not an empirical oracle.
+
+The body-sensitivity check materially changes the executed loop term to
+`result = result * factorial + 1` while retaining the original summary. Fresh
+`kprove` execution exits `1` with `WarnStuckClaimState` and the expected false
+equality between:
+
+```text
+productAfter(..., R * (F * I) + 1)
+productAfter(..., R * (F * I))
+```
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `evidence/04_adequacy.sh`
+- `evidence/04_adequacy.log` (exit `0`)
+- `evidence/04_witnesses.k`
+- `evidence/05_body_sensitivity.sh`
+- `evidence/05_body_sensitivity.log` (the negative K command exits `1`; the
+  validation wrapper exits `0`)
+
+## 5. Rule-by-rule static soundness review
+
+### Exhaustive inventory
+
+`evidence/05_rule_inventory.py` inventories the assembled semantics, all 24
+helper K files, `verification.k`, and `spec.k`. It records the complete
+normalized source text, location, attributes, and audit disposition of every:
+
+- 229 syntax declaration blocks;
+- 699 ordinary/equational rules;
+- 5 evaluation contexts;
+- 1 configuration;
+- 2 reachability claims.
+
+There are 936 records. The inventory includes all function/total declarations,
+all 45 rule priority attributes, all concrete and no-evaluator declarations,
+all `owise` rules, and both macro kinds. There are no source
+`[simplification]` or `[functional]` declarations. The complete enumeration is
+in `evidence/05_rule_inventory.log`; the accompanying static scans are in
+`evidence/05_static_checks.log`. Both wrappers exit `0`.
+
+### Used construct/rule map
+
+| Submitted construct | Fixed declarations and operational path |
+|---|---|
+| `Module`, statement lists | `syntax.k`; `core.k` `#loadAll`, head sequencing, empty sequence |
+| `FuncDef`, `Params` | `functions.k` ordinary closure creation |
+| `Call(Name(...), N)` | `core.k` name lookup; `call.k` callee then left-to-right argument evaluation and closure dispatch |
+| parameter binding | `functions.k` plain-frame `#bindP` |
+| integer literals and names | `core.k` literal and plain-scope lookup |
+| `Assign` | `syntax.k` RHS strictness; `controls.k` plain current-scope update |
+| `BinOp("*",...)`, `BinOp("+",...)` | `syntax.k` `seqstrict(2,3)`; `operators.k` dispatch; `int.k` exact integer equations |
+| `Compare(...,"<=")` | two `operators.k` evaluation contexts, then `int.k` `<=Int` |
+| `While` | `controls.k` `While -> #while`, guard evaluation, `#whileCond`, body, and recurring `#loopLbl` |
+| `Return` | `syntax.k` strict value evaluation; `functions.k` return, frame pop, environment restoration, and frame deallocation |
+
+This path uses unbounded K integers, not floats or machine integers. Evaluation
+order is the translator's AST order plus the supplied `strict`/`seqstrict`
+attributes and explicit comparison/call contexts: RHS before assignment,
+binary operands left-to-right, comparison left then right, callee before
+arguments, and arguments left-to-right.
+
+The only state changes are the module function binding, callee frame
+allocation, parameter/local map writes, stack push/pop, environment switch,
+and frame deallocation. Heap and exception cells remain unchanged. Return
+discards the remainder of the callee body, then restores the exact saved
+continuation; this matches the submitted control flow.
+
+### Overlaps, priorities, opaque values, and proof-local rules
+
+`verification.k` contributes exactly:
+
+- two `[function,total]` integer symbols;
+- four guarded equations;
+- no priority, simplification, concrete, opaque/no-evaluator, `Call`, `While`,
+  `Return`, or other operational rule.
+
+For each summary, `I > N` and `I <= N` are disjoint and exhaustive over K
+integers. The base equation returns the existing accumulator. The step equation
+increments `I`, uses exactly the program's new factorial in the product update,
+and decreases `max(N-I+1,0)`. The two functions are truthful definitional
+summaries. They do not match any MPY AST or any configuration cell and therefore
+are not operational bridges.
+
+The fixed semantics has 45 explicit priority rules. Every one was inspected.
+On this path:
+
+- cell-reference lookup/write priorities require `"$cells"` or a `cellRef`,
+  neither of which can occur in the ordinary submitted closure frame;
+- heap dereference rules require `ref`, while the program creates only integer
+  values and no heap objects;
+- list, tuple, dict, string-method, sort, assertion, and subscript priorities
+  require constructors absent from `solution.mpy`;
+- math and MD5 call interceptions require an `Attribute` callee with fixed
+  names, disjoint from `Call(Name("special_factorial"),...)`;
+- the generic call and comparison `owise` rules therefore select the intended
+  plain closure and integer paths.
+
+The fixed tree contains opaque/no-evaluator primitives for floats, sorting,
+MD5, and other tasks. None appears in `solution.mpy`, either claim, either
+summary, or any reachable value/cell. No proof conclusion depends on an
+interpretation of those symbols. Likewise, LLVM compilation reports six
+non-exhaustive totality warnings in unused fixed helpers:
+`mapStrVS`, `floorFI`, `toF`, `ceilF`, `joinCodes`, and `valSeqAt`. Their
+constructors cannot be reached by this integer-only program. `[total]` does not
+create a task answer, and no warned helper contributes to claim closure.
+
+I make no unsound-rule finding. In particular, I found no rule capable of
+enabling a false conclusion on any allowed positive-integer execution. The
+supplied semantics is intentionally only a Python subset outside this
+dependency slice; rules for unused language features are not evidence for or
+against this theorem. Within the reachable slice, configuration, evaluation
+order, scope updates, call/return, loop control, and integer operations match
+the program and ordinary mathematics.
+
+## 6. Fresh non-vacuity test
+
+I did not reuse the candidate's `spec-vacuity.k`. The reviewer-authored
+`evidence/06_false_result.k` keeps the exact program and loop invariant but
+changes the entry destination from:
+
+```text
+productAfter(1, N, 1, 1)
+```
+
+to:
+
+```text
+productAfter(1, N, 1, 1) + N
+```
+
+This is false throughout the precondition because `N >= 1`. The explicit
+satisfying witness `N=4` has canonical/candidate result `288` but mutated
+destination `292`.
+
+Commands and results:
+
+```bash
+kprove audit-false-result.k \
+  --definition audit-verification-kompiled \
+  --spec-module AUDIT-FALSE-RESULT \
+  --dry-run
+# exit 0: mutation parses and builds
+
+kprove audit-false-result.k \
+  --definition audit-verification-kompiled \
+  --spec-module AUDIT-FALSE-RESULT
+# exit 1
+```
+
+The failure is a meaningful `WarnStuckClaimState`, not a parser error, timeout,
+or unrelated crash. Its residual requires the impossible equality:
+
+```text
+productAfter(2, N, 1, 1) + N
+#Equals
+productAfter(2, N, 1, 1)
+```
+
+and retains `N >= 1`. Evidence:
+`evidence/06_false_result.k`, `evidence/06_nonvacuity.sh`, and
+`evidence/06_nonvacuity.log` (validation wrapper exit `0`).
+
+## 7. Proven versus assumed accounting
+
+### What the successful reachability proof establishes
+
+For every K integer `N >= 1`, from the fully specified normal module
+configuration in `SPEC.special-factorial`, fixed MPY execution:
+
+1. loads the exact trusted-regenerated submitted function;
+2. resolves and calls that exact binding with `N`;
+3. evaluates every initialization, guard, lookup, multiplication, addition,
+   assignment, loop-control step, and return in the submitted body;
+4. restores the caller configuration with no exception and exit code zero;
+5. leaves the returned K computation exactly
+   `productAfter(1,N,1,1)`.
+
+The proved loop circularity universally connects fixed execution of the exact

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u

review=/audit-output/REVIEW.md

test "$(tail -n 2 "$review")" = $'VERDICT: PASS\nLEGITIMACY: LEGIT'
marker_status=$?
printf 'exact_final_marker_status=%s\n' "$marker_status"
printf 'verdict_marker_count='
rg -c '^VERDICT:' "$review"
printf 'legitimacy_marker_count='
rg -c '^LEGITIMACY:' "$review"

printf '%s\n' '--- authored script syntax ---'
for script in /audit-output/evidence/*.sh; do
  bash -n "$script" || exit 1
done
printf 'bash_syntax_status=0\n'
python3 - <<'PY'
import ast
import pathlib

for path in sorted(pathlib.Path("/audit-output/evidence").glob("*.py")):
    ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), filename=str(path))
print("python_ast_parse_status=0")
PY

printf '%s\n' '--- material wrapper log statuses ---'
for log in \
  /audit-output/evidence/01_provenance_final.log \
  /audit-output/evidence/01_trace_summary.log \
  /audit-output/evidence/02_program_fidelity.log \
  /audit-output/evidence/03_reconstruct.log \
  /audit-output/evidence/04_adequacy.log \
  /audit-output/evidence/05_body_sensitivity.log \
  /audit-output/evidence/05_rule_inventory.log \
  /audit-output/evidence/05_static_checks.log \
  /audit-output/evidence/06_nonvacuity.log
do
  printf '%s: ' "$(basename "$log")"
  tail -n 1 "$log"
  rg -q 'COMMAND_EXIT_CODE="0"' "$log" || exit 1
done

printf '%s\n' '--- evidence and review hashes ---'
sha256sum "$review" /audit-output/evidence/*

exit "$marker_status"
